children: Kenya’s economy advanced by 5.1% year-on-year in Q2 2026, matching Q1 growth and maintaining its strongest pace since the fourth quarter of 2024 despite persistent global headwinds.
The expansion was mainly supported by stronger performance across services and key infrastructure-related sectors.
Electricity and water supply expanded by 7.7%, while accommodation and food services grew by 7.4%, reflecting continued strength in tourism-related activity.
Information and communication increased by 7.2%, followed by financial and insurance activities (6.1%), construction (6%) and transportation and storage (4.4%).
The agriculture, forestry and fishing sector, a key pillar of the economy, rose by 3.5%, down from 3.8% in Q1 and 4% in Q2 2025, partly reflecting the early end of the long rains.
On a seasonally adjusted basis, GDP rose by 1.2% quarter-on-quarter, following a 1.3% increase in the previous period.

title: Kenya Economy Maintains Robust Growth
